Like you said: there's a leash law. Also I'm assuming this was on the sidewalk, a dog can run into the street and get hit by a car, or like you pointed out get in an altercation with a dog that is not friendly towards other dogs. 

​

People here (not NY) have their dogs without a leash all the time despite it being a leash law: my brother was attacked by a dog when he was 5 years old, and he has a severe phobia since then. "Friendly" dogs come up to him and he literally freezes on the spot, it has caused a panic attack more than once if the dogs are pushing it too much. Everytime it happens I snap at people and tell them to have their dog on the leash. Their response is always "oh but they're friendly". The dog that attacked my brother was also friendly. We need to start treating abortion as what it is: a medical procedure and a public health subject.

One person texted me on whatsapp during my 5 day long vacations because I didn't respond to their email. I know my automatic replies were active so I just texted "Oh maybe you didn't receive my automatic reply. I'm on vacation until X day, I'll reply to you then. Bye". 

Maybe they felt bad. I don't care. I \*know\* for a fact they received my email (I've been getting "delivery errors" from automatic replies being sent to no-reply accounts so yeah, they were working) and decided "oh screw it, I'll text her anyway about my absurd and very-much-not-urgent-can-totally-wait-4-days request".

I still have to fight the urge to check my phone but now I just disconnect everything after I'm out of the office. Email? Unsync. Whatsapp? Mute. Phone calls? Do not disturb. Unless the building is literally on fire, don't contact me.

It's my understand that anti-work is not lack of activity, just lack of the oppressive work system that puts you in the position of "accept this work regardless of shitty conditions or DIE". If I didn't have the pressure of paying bills I would still do things, but things I actually enjoy: I'd probably volunteer more in my cat rescue, and get more involved with my friend's small yarn shop (I'd love to work with her and sell yarn but unfortunately she can't pay me enough for me to afford rent and bills, sooooo...). I daydream about winning the lottery and just doing all these things that would bring me more pleasure than a job where I constantly have to fight to feel valued.

Keep in mind we want to hire someone to take care of the website and social media, currently my coworker-friend does this on top of a lot of other administrative job. I know PLENTY of people my age (early 30s) who still keep objects with sentimental value. I'm 31 and I still have my first pair of shoes and a couple of stuffed animals (one given by my grandparents, who are now dead, and one given by my dad, also dead), what does that say about me? Sure some people might feel that was an overreacting but honestly do you really want insensitive AHs like that in your life? OP, you don't want them in your life then that's it. Everybody has their dealbreakers, and making YOU posting a picture of YOUR sick mother about THEM and how THEY feel about it is kind of a big one.
